sections.h2: Which Garrard County office answers which tax question?
sections.html:
The PVA owns the value, and the sheriff owns the bill. The county's own site stresses that the PVA neither sets rates nor collects, and the sheriff's page says the sheriff never assesses property, so an argument over the figure goes to one office and a question about paying goes to the other.

Both sit at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster. The PVA answers at (859) 792-3291 on weekdays during the 8 to 4 day, and the sheriff's number is (859) 792-3591. Think of the PVA as a state office with a local address. State revenue officials supervise it, and every parcel is valued at full fair cash value as of January 1.

The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts. The list covers state and county levies, school districts, and special districts for things like fire protection and libraries. Bills go out on October 1 every year with instructions on due dates, penalties, mortgage-company payment and ways to pay. The County Clerk, at 15 Public Square, Suite 5, records deeds and helps notify and collect on delinquent bills.

sections.h2: What should I know about Garrard County before selling?
sections.html:
Garrard County is in east-central Kentucky and has 230 square miles of land. Rolling Bluegrass country fills most of it, and the southeast corner near Cartersville falls in the Knobs. Lancaster, the seat and the only city, started as a cluster of log cabins in 1776, and the county was formed in 1796 from parts of Lincoln, Mercer and Madison counties, making it the 25th in the state.

Lexington is about 28 miles north. Outside Lancaster you find Paint Lick, Bryantsville, Buckeye, Cartersville, Davis Town and Hyattsville, and the 2020 census classed all residents as rural. Camp Dick Robinson, the first Federal base south of the Ohio River in the Civil War, was in the county. A tobacco heritage festival takes place every September, and voters ended the county's dry status on November 7, 2023.

The county has gained residents quickly, and the average commute is long.

  • Population: 18,207 in the 2025 estimate, up 7.4 percent from 2020.
  • Typical home value in the 2020 to 2024 survey: $204,900.
  • Owner-occupied share: 79.9 percent, the highest among Floyd, Franklin, Gallatin and Garrard.
  • Average commute: 33.1 minutes, the longest among those four.
  • New-home permits in 2025: 0.
  • Median gross rent: $794. Median household income: $63,087.

In 2020 the census counted 7,254 housing units, 9.2 percent of them empty, and 6,584 households. With no permits recorded in 2025, sales are mostly of existing houses and acreage.

The local economy is small and heavily self-employed. The Census Bureau lists 251 employer businesses in 2023 with 1,654 jobs and a $71.4 million payroll, against 1,572 businesses with no employees. Retail sales were about $80.8 million in 2022, or $4,600 per resident, a fraction of the Franklin County figure of $19,603, a much smaller per-person total. Just over half of adults (54.7 percent) are working or looking for work, and the Census Bureau shows 18.7 percent with a four-year degree. The county government is run by a fiscal court of a judge executive and five magistrates, and the courthouse in Lancaster is one of the oldest in continuous use in Kentucky.

sections.h2: When is the Garrard County bill due, and what is the discount?
sections.html:
The sheriff expects payment by December 31, and bills leave on October 1, so the early-payment window is about a month long. Under KRS 134.015, paying the entire bill by November 1 trims 2 percent. A January payment costs an extra 5 percent, and later ones cost 10 percent.

When statewide mailing runs late, Revenue can substitute a short calendar: a month with the discount, a month at face, then a month with the 5 percent charge. The tax is a personal debt of the person who held title on January 1, which matters for a sale that closes early in the year.

sections.h2: How much does a late Garrard County bill cost?
sections.html:
A lot more. A bill still open on April 15 leaves the sheriff for the County Clerk, and a lien is recorded against the parcel. The state illustrates the climb with a $1,000 bill and a sheriff commission assumed at 4 percent, so your own totals will differ.

State worked example: what an unpaid $1,000 tax bill costs as weeks pass (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
Payment dateAmount owed
The day the sheriff hands it over, with penalty, add-on and commission$1,254.00
Within a week of the handover$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first letter$1,611.30
In May, a second month of interest$1,627.61
In June, once the newspaper ad has run$1,659.90

Interest is 1 percent per month. A 30-day notice and a second notice come from the county attorney, and the clerk's sale is set 90 to 135 days after transfer. When a certificate sells to an outside buyer, you owe that buyer plus its additional fees.

sections.h2: What should a Garrard County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Treat the tax bill as part of the sale paperwork. Because the sheriff mails bills in October and the debt belongs to whoever held the property on January 1, a house that closes in spring or summer may still have a bill outstanding in the seller's name.

  • Phone the sheriff's office at (859) 792-3591 for the amount due on the parcel.
  • Ask the County Clerk at (859) 792-3071 how to record the deed, since the clerk's office archives deeds and mortgages.
  • Tell the PVA at (859) 792-3291 who the new owner is so later notices and any exemption follow the right person.
  • Keep the paid receipt with your closing file, because the buyer's title search will otherwise show the balance as open.

An owner behind on taxes and facing repairs on an older farmhouse may also weigh a direct sale to a buyer that closes as-is, which avoids carrying the bill through a long listing.

sections.h2: How can a Garrard County owner appeal?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA, then file with the County Clerk. The roll is open for 13 days beginning in early May, and the conference comes first. File by the end of the next business day after viewing closes.

A local board of assessment appeals then meets about four to five weeks later and rules on documented evidence: comparable listings, construction costs, photographs. It must give written reasons for a change. A paid representative must be an attorney, appraiser or another approved professional carrying your written authorization.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption for Garrard County owners?
sections.html:
Seniors and totally disabled owners can subtract $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA on Stanford Street. At the county's typical home value of $204,900, the taxable amount would be $155,800.

To show age, bring a birth certificate, license or passport. A seller who has held the exemption should tell the PVA after closing so it ends at that address.

faqs.q: When do Garrard County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: They are mailed on October 1 each year, according to the Garrard County Sheriff. Payment in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount.

faqs.q: Who should I call if a Garrard County tax value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the Garrard County PVA at (859) 792-3291. The sheriff's office says it never assesses value and refers those questions to the PVA.

faqs.q: Where is the Garrard County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster, KY 40444, with a phone at (859) 792-3591. The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts.

faqs.q: What changes for Garrard County taxes still open on April 15?
faqs.a: The bill moves to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent per month starts, and clerk and attorney commissions follow.

faqs.q: What is the Garrard County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, taken off the assessed value of a home owned by a senior or a totally disabled person.
